primaryDecision: Stabilize a practical Role & Authority toolkit with a small set of source/workflow records plus normalized derived projections. Do not create a second authority source-of-truth or a global authority hierarchy.

sourceOrWorkflowRecords: RoleAssignmentChangeReceipt when explicit appointment/replacement workflow exists
sourceDerivedBoundary.reason: Authority can originate from different Game-owned rules, role templates, constitutive practice, direct grants, delegation or local policy. Cross-Game stabilization should normalize effective authority for tooling without duplicating local source truth.

RoleAssignmentRecord.purpose: Durably identify that an occupant currently or historically occupies a role in a declared practice/scope without implying authority by role label alone.
forbiddenImplications: role label determines capability or control
RoleAssignmentRecord.currentness: Current if the query time/context is inside the assignment validity and no authoritative ending/replacement relation invalidates it.
RoleAssignmentRecord.persistence: Persist when assignment identity/history/coordination matters; otherwise a local static configuration may compile into the same view.

ScopedAuthorityEdge.purpose: Provide one cross-Game effective authority query shape over heterogeneous local authority sources.
ScopedAuthorityEdge.operationKeyRule: Use namespaced open operation keys owned by the GameForm/practice; do not freeze one exhaustive universal enum.
ScopedAuthorityEdge.scopeRule: scopeRefs resolve through owner-local scope semantics. No universal scope tree/lattice is assumed; multiple scope dimensions may be incomparable.
ScopedAuthorityEdge.truthRule: The edge is a projection of effective current authority, not an independent authority grant by mere existence in a cache/UI.
forbiddenImplications: same holder identity implies same operation authority

AuthorityProfile.purpose: Compactly summarize one holder's current effective and conditional authority for Human/Agent inspection.
laws: absence of an edge is not metaphysical impossibility
authority check is not full GDF1 action admission

AgentAuthorityManifest.purpose: Give an Agent a compact current answer to what it may bind/change/decide within a particular context without forcing raw authority-graph reconstruction every turn.
AgentAuthorityManifest.stalenessRule: A manifest is a derived snapshot. Any relevant role assignment, authority source, scope/currentness or separation-policy change invalidates or changes its authorityStateDigest.
AgentAuthorityManifest.criticalLaw: AgentAuthorityManifest != legal action set != capability set != GameAction admission. GDF1 admission remains separate.
forbiddenImplications: manifest allows hidden authority not in sources
stale manifest remains valid after authority state changes

RoleCausalAccessProfile.purpose: Expose what an occupant/role can perceive, communicate, contribute to, influence, control and authoritatively bind without collapsing those dimensions.
laws: authority != causal ability to realize outcome
RoleCausalAccessProfile.persistence: Derived by default from F7/GDF1/role/authority state.

ParticipationAuthorityTopology.purpose: Visualize/debug the scoped relationship among entities, role assignments, causal access and authority without asserting a hierarchy.

AuthoritySeparationPolicy.purpose: Allow a GamePractice to configure separation-of-duties constraints without claiming they are universal semantic laws.
AuthoritySeparationPolicy.law: Separation constraints filter/evaluate effective authority in context; they do not create a universal authority hierarchy or imply all games need dual control.

DelegationGrantRecord.purpose: Represent a durable scoped transfer/grant of authority when a practice actually delegates authority rather than merely approving one action.
admissionRules: grantor must have current authority to delegate this operation/scope, not merely authority to perform the underlying operation
delegated scope cannot exceed what the admitted delegation basis authorizes
subdelegation is not implicit and requires its own delegation authority/basis
revocation authority is not inferred merely from grantor identity unless the practice policy says so
expiry/revocation ends current effect but does not erase grant history
DelegationGrantRecord.currentEngineeringMapping: Station Zero Team AuthorityGrant is proposal/context/world-bound one-shot action authorization consumed on use; it should not be generalized as DelegationGrant merely because its local type contains the word Grant.

AppointmentReplacementRecord.purpose: Audit/coordinate explicit appointment or replacement workflows while keeping RoleAssignment as the actual practical relation.
laws: replacement ends/supersedes an assignment and may create a new assignment
replacement does not automatically transfer direct entity-bound authority
record is optional when a simple static role assignment is enough

ActorProfileRole.finding: Useful Station Zero role label/mandate input, but it lacks generic assignment identity/currentness/provenance and must not be generalized into cross-Game RoleAssignment by type alias alone.

AuthorityDecision.finding: Represents a contextual permit/require-human/deny decision for one action candidate; it is not the same thing as a durable ScopedAuthorityEdge.

AuthorityGrant.finding: Bound to proposalId/actionCandidateId/contextDigest/worldDigest, expires and is consumed once. This is excellent currentness binding but is not generic DelegationGrant because it transfers no reusable authority operation to the actor.

AuthorityPolicyMode.finding: autonomous/supervised/locked and require-human semantics are Station Zero-specific. GPR1 should preserve the pattern of policy evaluation while not freezing Human as the universal escalation authority.

candidateAllowed.finding: Demonstrates why Authority != GameActionAdmission: authority policy/grant is one input to whether an action candidate proceeds; capability, legality/current World state remain separate Game responsibilities.

implementationDecision.reason: GPR1 establishes practical contracts and source/view boundaries. A later consumption/audit round should map these contracts onto actual product consumers before creating generic library types or migrations.
implementationCandidates: only later, source records if a real cross-Game consumer requires them

nextRound.name: GPR2 — Case Determination & Contestability Toolkit
nextRound.reason: R0 already ranked P2 immediately behind P1, and GPR1 now supplies the role/authority substrate required to rebuild determination records, review/appeal workflows and decision lineage safely. This is practical reconstruction ordering, not a new Deep Foundation admission.
